title: Feature boundary policy — independent verification + dependency boundaries, not file count
body:
Locked policy for all future plans (not just F1):

> Feature boundaries are determined by independent verification and dependency boundaries, not by file count or perceived size. Cross-repo changes, schema/version changes, lifecycle gate behavior, and dogfood proof points are separate features by default. A feature must have meaningful acceptance evidence and a failure mode that can be triaged without reopening unrelated work.

Application to F1: 5 features split because each has its own boundary —

- F001 (cross-repo + schema/version/tag boundary, releasable independently as agent-conventions v1.4.0).
- F002 (mechanical import boundary; isolates upstream consumption from local behavior changes).
- F003 (core local logic, testable after F001/F002).
- F004 (lifecycle gate behavior depending on F003 outputs; different failure mode from auditor logic — wrong gate placement vs wrong findings).
- F005 (operator-judged dogfood proof; can fail without invalidating F001–F004 logic).

Reason: 'F1 is large' is not a justification — that's about size. The justification is *triability*: if F004's gate placement turns out wrong, you don't have to reopen F001's schema work. If F005's dogfood reveals the prompt needs tuning, you don't have to reopen F002's subtree pull. Each feature has a clean failure mode that doesn't drag the others.

How to apply: Plans going forward should use this policy at decomposition time. Future plan-authoring tools (e.g., F1's sufficiency auditor itself) can cite this D-entry when surfacing 'this feature should be split' findings.

title: `goal_type` is top-level Plan field; objective_contract is referenced via `links.objective_contract`, NOT inline embedding
body:
Locked schema design:

- `Plan.goal_type: GoalType | None = None` — top-level optional field.
- `Links.objective_contract: str | None = None` — path reference, follows the existing `links.{features,decisions,audits_dir,evidence_dir}` pattern.
- Validator rule: when `goal_type ∈ {parity, new_feature, migration, incident}`, the plan MUST declare `links.objective_contract`, the file at that path MUST exist, and it MUST validate against `ObjectiveContract`.

Reason for `links` reference (not inline embedding):

- Plan model already has `Links` for path refs to features/decisions/etc. Reusing it is consistent.
- Objective contracts can be substantial (full user_journeys list with state/wiring/edge cases per journey). Inlining bloats plan.md frontmatter beyond the existing pattern.
- Path reference makes the contract independently editable + version-trackable in git.
- Path reference avoids YAML/JSON nesting awkwardness in plan.md frontmatter.

Reason for top-level `goal_type` (not inside the contract):

- The validator must know `goal_type` BEFORE deciding whether to require an objective_contract. If goal_type were inside the contract, the validator can't tell missing-but-needed from not-needed.
- Top-level + optional + default-None preserves backward compat (existing plans don't have goal_type, validator skips the check).

How to apply: F001 step 4 + step 5 codify the schema additions. F001 acceptance #3 + #4 lock the field placement.

title: F1 self-bootstrap — F1 does NOT declare its own goal_type
body:
F1 introduces the objective_contract machinery. The natural question: does F1 itself need an objective_contract?

Locked answer: **No.** F1 leaves `goal_type` unset on its own plan.md frontmatter.

Reason: backward compat covers the bootstrap. Default-None goal_type means the validator's new rule does not engage. F1 is in the same boat as Plans A–E + F0 — none declare goal_type, all continue to validate green. No special exemption needed; the design is self-bootstrapping.

The alternative (declaring `goal_type: infra` for F1) would be defensible but unnecessary. `infra` doesn't require a contract per the §4 applicability rule, so the validator wouldn't engage anyway. Leaving goal_type unset is the simpler form.

How to apply: F1's plan.md does not declare goal_type. F002 acceptance #3 verifies F1 itself validates green post-pull as backward-compat evidence.

title: agent-conventions semver = v1.4.0 (MINOR — additive functionality)
body:
Plan E was v1.3.0 → v1.3.1 (PATCH — bug fix in dispatch logic, no schema/model changes).

F1 is qualitatively different:

- Adds new schema file (`objective_contract.schema.json`).
- Adds new Pydantic model (`objective_contract_model.py`).
- Extends `plan.schema.json` with new optional fields (`goal_type`, `links.objective_contract`).
- Extends `validate.py` with new validation rule.

This is **additive functionality** consumers (DontPanic, Glam, SpinDineSwift) may want to opt into deliberately. Semver classification: MINOR.

v1.3.1 → v1.4.0.

Backward compat preserved: existing plans without goal_type validate green under v1.4.0. The new schema only engages when goal_type is declared. Consumers can adopt at their own pace.

How to apply: F001 step 9 hardcodes the bump. F001 acceptance #8 locks the version string.

title: F005 'materially correct' judgment is operator-reviewed with written disposition per plan
body:
Per Goal Governance V1 §9 F1.7: 'auditor must identify at least one materially correct gap class in each.' What counts as 'materially correct' is operator-judged, not a synthetic test assertion.

Locked F005 close-out requirement:

- Operator writes a markdown disposition file for Spin & Dine: `evidence/spin-and-dine-disposition.md`.
- Operator writes a markdown disposition file for Glam: `evidence/glam-disposition.md`.
- Each disposition has required sections: (a) PASS/FAIL verdict on materially-correct judgment; (b) specific findings the operator considers materially correct (cited by finding ID); (c) specific findings the operator considers noise/false-positives; (d) recommendations for sufficiency prompt or schema revisions if PASS=False.

Reason: programmatic 'materially correct' would push interpretive judgment into model behavior — exactly the wrong direction for governance. The point of F005 is to test whether the auditor's findings match operator intuition about what gaps actually matter. Operator-written disposition is the proof.

How to apply: F005 step 7 + acceptance #4 + #5 lock the written-disposition requirement.

title: Cross-vendor goal auditor by default; resolve via agent_manifest/config; NO hardcoded vendor
body:
Per Goal Governance V1 §5 vendor policy: goal auditor must be different vendor from feature implementer by default.

Locked F003 implementation:

- `_resolve_goal_auditor_agent(implementer_agent: str | None) -> str` reads from agent_manifest.
- Default behavior when implementer is Claude: returns Codex (today's expected non-Claude vendor).
- Default behavior when implementer is Codex: returns Claude.
- Same-vendor goal audit allowed only with explicit operator override (Goal Governance V1 §5 quota fallback). Without override, raises ValueError.

**No hardcoded vendor name in the function body.** The resolution path is configurable via agent_manifest. Today's expected default is Codex when Claude implements, but that's policy-driven, not code-driven.

Reason: vendor independence is the property that makes goal auditing trustworthy. Hardcoding Codex would make F003 brittle to future agent_manifest changes (e.g., Gemini becoming the goal_auditor default for some project, or quota constraints forcing a fallback). The manifest is the single source of truth.

How to apply: F003 step 4 implements the resolver via manifest reads. F003 acceptance #3 locks the no-hardcoded-vendor invariant. Tests cover both the happy path and the same-vendor-without-override ValueError case.

title: F005 direct path — dogfood judgment is interpretive, volley would be noise
body:
F005 is the operator-judged dogfood proof. A volley would dispatch an auditor to review whether Spin & Dine's objective_contract was 'well-written' — but that question is interpretive (what counts as well-written?) and the volley would mostly produce findings about prose quality, not real correctness signal.

Locked: F005 ships direct. Same logic as Plans A, C-F001/F002, D, E, F0 — mechanical/judgment-driven slices don't volley.

F001/F002/F003/F004 are also direct (mechanical schema, subtree pull, module implementation, lifecycle wiring respectively).

Reason: volley quota is unjustified for the entire F1 plan. The proof points are deterministic acceptance (F001-F004) + operator disposition (F005). Neither needs an adversarial auditor to surface defects.

How to apply: F1's `loop_caps.max_iterations: 1` + `agents_required: [claude, codex]` (codex listed because F003's auditor uses it at runtime, not because F1 itself volleys). Per the `meta_plan_actions_human_vs_orchestrator` memory: drafting/locking/close-out for direct slices stays human-brokered.

title: F005 stays in F1 — splitting would let F1 ship without proving the failure mode
body:
Tempting alternative: split F005 into a separate Plan F1b — F1a ships F001-F004 as the 'mechanical machinery' part, F1b ships the dogfood as the 'proof' part.

Locked: F005 stays in F1. Reason per the boundary policy in D001:

- F005 is the proof that F1 actually addresses the failure mode it exists for. Splitting it lets F1 ship without that proof.
- F005 has a clean failure mode that doesn't drag F001-F004: if F005 fails because the prompt needs tuning, F003 can be adjusted without reopening F001's schema. The boundary policy permits this.
- But splitting would let F1 close as 'mechanical machinery shipped' without demonstrating the machinery actually works on real plans. That's the failure mode Goal Governance V1 §9 F1.7 explicitly guards against ('Synthetic test fixtures alone do not satisfy F1').

The right boundary is feature-within-plan (F005 is a feature with a clean failure mode), not plan-within-arc (Plan F1b would let F1 close prematurely).

How to apply: F005 lives in F1's features.json. F1 close-out is gated on F005 dispositions per D010.

title: Cross-repo two-commit boundary — F001 in agent-conventions, F002+ in DontPanic
body:
Mirroring Plan E pattern:

- F001 ships as ONE commit in agent-conventions (schema + model + validator + version bump + tag v1.4.0). Commit lives in `$HOME/Documents/GitHub/agent-conventions/`.
- F002 ships as TWO commits in DontPanic (subtree-pull squash + merge), per `git subtree pull --squash` mechanics.
- F003 ships as ONE commit in DontPanic (auditor module + tests + close-out memo).
- F004 ships as ONE commit in DontPanic (gate wiring + tests + close-out memo).
- F005 ships as ONE commit in DontPanic (dogfood plans + dispositions + close-out memo + features.json passes flips).

Not allowed:

- Bundling F001 + F002 (impossible anyway since they're in different repos, but worth stating).
- Modifying `claude/shared/` in DontPanic OUTSIDE the F002 subtree-pull operation. F002's diff for `claude/shared/**` MUST exactly match the upstream v1.4.0 contents.
- F003/F004/F005 touching `claude/shared/` at all (no second subtree pull mid-plan).

Reason: independent rollback. Same logic as Plan E D006. If F005 dogfood reveals F003's prompt is wrong, F003 can be reverted independently of F001/F002. If F004's gate placement is wrong, F004 reverts without dragging F001-F003.

How to apply: each feature's close-out memo records its commit SHA. F005 close-out memo cross-references all 5 commits.

title: F1 close-out gate (strengthened) — fails if EITHER Spin & Dine OR Glam dogfood case fails
body:
Original wording (Goal Governance V1 §9 F1.7): 'If it misses both, F1 fails.'

Strengthened wording locked here:

> F1 close-out fails unless the sufficiency auditor surfaces at least one materially correct gap class for Spin & Dine **and** at least one materially correct gap class for Glam. If either dogfood case fails, the sufficiency prompt, objective-contract schema, or decomposition rules must be revised before F1 can close.

Reason for strengthening: 'misses both' lets F1 close on partial proof. Either case being missed is a real signal — Spin & Dine and Glam represent different failure modes (parity matrix vs integration coverage), and the auditor needs to handle both. If only one case lands, the missing case might be the one that matters in production.

Locked failure response, in priority order:

1. **Sufficiency prompt revision** (in F003) — if the auditor is asking the wrong questions or producing the wrong output shape.
2. **Objective-contract schema revision** (in F001 — would require subtree re-pull) — if the contract fields are insufficient to surface the missed gap class.
3. **Decomposition rules revision** (in this F005 step itself) — if the synthetic plan's features.json was authored such that the auditor 'correctly' found nothing wrong (i.e., the dogfood was set up to pass trivially).

F005 close-out memo records the diagnosis if either case fails.

How to apply: F005 acceptance #6 + #7 lock the per-plan materially-correct requirement. F005 acceptance #8 locks the gating + diagnosis behavior.

title: F004 sufficiency gate applies to every plan-lock path, not just CLI draft → active
body:
Locked: F004's `enforce_sufficiency_gate()` must apply to every path that transitions a plan into a locked state. Surveyed lock paths:

- CLI: `dontpanic plan lock <plan-dir>` (or whatever the canonical command is).
- Plan validator: at next validation run, if status was edited manually from `draft` to `active`/`ready_for_audit`/etc.
- MCP server: any future programmatic lock path through the MCP tools.
- Direct status-flip helpers in `plan_loader.py` (if any).

F004 step 2 surveys the actual surface and documents in the F004 close-out memo. F004 step 5 wires the gate into all identified paths.

Reason: gate-once-per-CLI-path leaks. If an operator manually edits plan.md status from draft to active, the gate should still engage at the next validation run. If a future MCP tool adds a new lock path, that path should also engage the gate. Single-point-of-enforcement (e.g., always gating in CLI) creates bypass paths.

The operator override (`--ignore-sufficiency-findings <reason>`) remains the only legitimate bypass — and it's recorded in evidence, not silent.

How to apply: F004 step 2 (survey) + step 5 (wiring) + acceptance #2 (every-lock-path coverage) + close-out memo (enumerated lock paths).

title: Lock signal — F1 plan shape
body:
Locked at 2026-05-05 lock turn. Operator's lock signal:

> The proposed F1 shape is directionally right, but the justification should not be '5 features because F1 is large.' It should be '5 features because there are 5 independently verifiable dependency boundaries.' Keep the split, and lock the feature-boundary policy in D001 so future plans do not hand-wave this.

Followed by per-question answers (Q1-Q8) and structural amendments (cross-repo boundary, F1 close-out wording strengthened, F004 rename to 'plan-lock sufficiency gate/check' covering every lock path).

Key amendments captured:

- D001 — boundary policy is locked, applies to future plans (not just F1).
- D002 — `links.objective_contract` (path ref), not inline.
- D005 — F005 dogfood requires written operator disposition per plan.
- D006 — no hardcoded vendor; resolve via manifest.
- D010 — strengthened gating wording (either case fails → F1 fails).
- D011 — F004 covers every lock path, not just CLI.

Any deviation from these terms during F001-F005 implementation requires an explicit D-entry amendment and operator re-confirmation (per the `scope_change_protocol` memory).

title: Project-agnostic invariant — Spin & Dine and Glam are dogfood examples only, NOT product-specific integrations
body:
Locked invariant for F1 and all future Goal Governance plans:

> Spin & Dine and Glam are F1 dogfood examples only. They are not product-specific integrations. F005 uses static, plan-local fixtures under F1 evidence. DontPanic code must remain project-agnostic; project names may appear only in dogfood fixture paths/content and close-out evidence.

Application to F1:

- F005 fixtures live at `docs/plans/2026-05-05-003-.../evidence/dogfood/{spin-and-dine,glam}/` — plan-local, NOT a top-level `dogfood/` directory.
- F005 does NOT read from external Spin & Dine / Glam / Styln repos. Fixtures are static curated content authored inside F1 evidence; reproducible without external state.
- F005 fixtures are realistic enough to surface real gap classes but treated as generic objective-contract examples, not coupled to actual project shapes.
- DontPanic code (anything under `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/`) MUST NOT contain project-name-specific behavior — no `spin_dine_*`, `glam_*`, `styln_*`, `creator_hub_*`, `android_parity_*` special cases. The product capability is general:
  - objective contract schema
  - text-only sufficiency auditor
  - plan-lock gate
  - goal-gap classification (F0)
  - evidence/disposition workflow
- Project names appear ONLY in (a) `evidence/dogfood/<project>/` fixture paths, (b) the content of those fixtures' `objective_contract.json` / `plan.md` / `features.json` files, (c) close-out evidence files (`evidence/<project>-disposition.md`, `f005-closeout-memo.md`).

Reason: DontPanic is product-agnostic infrastructure. Coupling it to specific projects would (a) break the 'called by, not specific to' positioning in PRODUCT.md / ECOSYSTEM.md; (b) make it harder to onboard new projects (each would need its own hardcoded path); (c) blur the boundary between dogfood-as-test and dogfood-as-feature. The dogfood proves the general system catches the kind of gaps the operator personally saw — not that DontPanic ships Spin & Dine support.

How to apply: F005 acceptance #11 includes a greppable assertion that `git diff --name-only` shows zero matches for project-named modules / classes / special cases in `scripts/`. F005 step 11 confirms no top-level `dogfood/` directory created. Future plans extending Goal Governance (F2 / Plan G / Plan H) inherit this invariant — they may add new dogfood fixtures inside their own evidence dirs, but never cross the project-agnostic line in product code.

title: F003 close-out — pre-impl sufficiency auditor module shipped, lock enforcement deferred to F004
body:
F003 sealed in DontPanic per the locked F1 dependency order (depends_on F002).

Boundary kept tight per the operator directive on this turn:
- zero changes under claude/shared/** (D009 two-commit cross-repo boundary preserved)
- no edits to nested_orchestration.py or any other existing module
- only two new files added: scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/sufficiency_auditor.py + the matching test module
- the v1.4.0 ObjectiveContract model is consumed via the F002 subtree import (claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/models/), never duplicated

Public surface of sufficiency_auditor.py:
- run_sufficiency_audit(plan_dir, *, implementer_agent=None, dispatch=None) -> list[SufficiencyFinding]
- SufficiencyFinding (Pydantic model) — severity validator reuses F0's _GOAL_GAP_SEVERITY_RANK
- SUFFICIENCY_GAP_CLASSES taxonomy (5 values: coverage_gap / missing_feature / wiring_gap / parity_gap / integration_gap)
- SufficiencyAuditError (subclasses ValueError)
- _resolve_goal_auditor_agent(plan_dir, implementer_agent=None) — reads project_config (D004 precedence), enforces D006 cross-vendor invariant

Cross-vendor (D006 / Goal Governance V1 §5) implementation:
- vendor names come exclusively from project_config.resolve_dispatch_defaults(); never hardcoded in this module
- same-vendor (auditor == implementer) is refused unless DONTPANIC_GOAL_AUDITOR_ALLOW_SAME_VENDOR is set truthy in the environment
- override channel is recorded as evidence by the caller, not silently consumed here

Lock enforcement (D011) deliberately deferred to F004:
- run_sufficiency_audit accepts a `dispatch` callable seam but raises if none is supplied (no default real-dispatch wiring)
- F004's plan-lock gate will pass a production dispatcher and decide what to do with the returned findings (refuse-to-lock vs --ignore-sufficiency-findings <reason> override)

Verification:
- 22 new tests, all green (covers the 9 step-8 cases plus extras for code-fence tolerance + non-array top-level rejection + fail-fast on contract-load before dispatch + same-vendor override happy path)
- full orchestrate suite: 1019 passed, 6 skipped (= 997 F002 baseline + 22 new). Zero regressions.
- ruff check + ruff format --check: clean (no UP035, no I001, no F401, no formatter diffs)
- python3 scripts/sanitization_check.py: 0 findings (756 files scanned)
- worktree boundary: zero diff to claude/shared/**, nested_orchestration.py, or other modules

How to apply: F004 begins next per dependency order (depends_on F003). F004 wires the lock gate that consumes evidence/goal-governance/pre_impl/sufficiency-findings.json and surveys every plan-lock path (CLI, validator, MCP, direct helpers) per D011. Operator override of the same-vendor invariant must be recorded in F004's lock-time evidence whenever set.
